partners.mechanism_chain: Phosphoglycerate kinase 1 (PGK1) (HGNC:9007) —DISRUPTS→ Glycolysis; Phosphofructokinase muscle (PFKM) (HGNC:8919) —DISRUPTS→ Glycolysis; Glycolysis —DECREASES→ ATP; ATP —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0003691); ATP —LEADS_TO→ Exercise intolerance (HP:0009132); ATP —LEADS_TO→ Myopathy (HP:0003198); ATP —LEADS_TO→ Hemolytic anemia (HP:0001880). Mutations in PGK1 (GSD-PGK1) and PFKM (GSD-VII) both impair the glycolytic pathway. This disruption leads to reduced ATP production, particularly impacting high-energy demanding tissues like muscle, resulting in shared phenotypes such as muscle weakness, exercise intolerance, and myopathy. Red blood cells, which rely solely on glycolysis, are also affected, leading to hemolytic anemia in both conditions.

partners.diseaseBName: non-spherocytic hemolytic anemia due to hexokinase deficiency
partners.mechanism_chain: Phosphoglycerate Kinase 1 (HGNC:9300) —DISRUPTS→ Glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-1435410); Glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-1435410) —DECREASES→ ATP (CHEBI:15378); Glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-1435410) —LEADS_TO→ Glycogen storage disease (MONDO:0010392); Hexokinase 1 (HGNC:4973) —DISRUPTS→ Glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-1435410); Glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-1435410) —DECREASES→ Glucose-6-phosphate (CHEBI:17793); Glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-1435410) —LEADS_TO→ Non-spherocytic hemolytic anemia (MONDO:0009340). Deficiency in PGK1 (Disease A) impairs a late step in glycolysis, reducing ATP production and impacting cellular function, leading to glycogen storage disease. Deficiency in HK1 (Disease B) impairs an early step in glycolysis, reducing glucose phosphorylation and thus overall glycolytic flux and ATP production, leading to non-spherocytic hemolytic anemia. Both defects converge on the disruption of the glycolytic pathway and consequently ATP production, impacting red blood cell viability and leading to distinct but related pathologies.

**Proposed mechanism:** Loss-of-function variant in PGK1 —DISRUPTS→ Phosphoglycerate kinase 1 (HGNC:9312); Phosphoglycerate kinase 1 (HGNC:9312) —DECREASES→ Glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-569337); Glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-569337) —DECREASES→ 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate (CHEBI:17497); 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate (CHEBI:17497) —LEADS_TO→ Glycerol-3-phosphate metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1433307); Glycerol-3-phosphate metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1433307) —LEADS_TO→ Hypoglycemia (HP:0001250); Loss-of-function variant in ALDOB —DISRUPTS→ Aldolase B (HGNC:266); Aldolase B (HGNC:266) —DECREASES→ Glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-569337); Glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-569337) —LEADS_TO→ Hepatomegaly (HP:0002293). Loss-of-function mutations in PGK1 disrupt glycolysis, leading to accumulation of 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate and impaired glycerol-3-phosphate metabolism, causing hypoglycemia. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in ALDOB disrupt glycolysis, leading to accumulation of fructose-1-phosphate (not explicitly modeled but implied by ALDOB's role) and downstream effects contributing to hepatomegaly and hypoglycemia.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of a pathogenic variant in a gene other than PGK1 or ALDOB that is singly responsible for either GSD-PGK1 or HFI, or demonstration that the shared phenotypes arise from completely independent molecular pathways not converging on glycolysis or glycerol-3-phosphate metabolism. _(variant: A common pathogenic variant (allele frequency > 0.1%) in either PGK1 or ALDOB in the general population.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared metabolic vulnerability of these diseases, particularly the central role of glycolysis, could reveal common therapeutic targets for managing hypoglycemia and other metabolic complications. Strategies aimed at restoring flux through glycolysis or alternative pathways for glucose production could be beneficial for both conditions.
